title: Gospel recording costs and refusing outside tapes
summary: McRae records his own groups, recalls refusing to release the Skyways' Savoy-made tape, and prefers to record artists himself.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

That's top albums what James Cleveland would turn out. You know, what we turn out, we probably wouldn't spend no more than maybe five the top -- five thousand, we did a live album.
We try to keep it down, you know. We couldn't run our overheard as much as Savoy's. They had more artists then we had.
We have to keep -- you always try to keep your overhead down according to the size of your company, you know.
There's a lot of companies -- I know they spend a lot of money on an album.
We make a choice not to put out anything that --
I generally record myself, the company don't record. Because this way, we know what we're getting.
Like, people send us tapes -- we wanna release this album or release this 45 and they wanna tape and it doesn't come up to the sound that you --
It was a group that I had, the Brooklyn Skyways. Was an incident where it came up where they
